title: Deterministic Scenario Runner for VPC/On-Prem Throughput & p95 Regression Detection
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Build a deterministic scenario runner that can synthesize and replay customer-like workloads inside Private/VPC/on-prem testbeds for tokens/sec, tail-latency (p95) tracking, and automated regression detection. The goal is to enable engineers and SREs to reproduce customer performance regressions with high fidelity without requiring a full customer snapshot. Key capabilities:

- Scenario authoring: ingest compressed traces and topology manifests and compile into deterministic scenarios with seeded RNG, request timing preservation, and option to inject synthetic jitter/packet loss.
- Environment synthesizer: lightweight network emulation layer that can replay latency and bandwidth profiles per-tenant using tc/NetEm or eBPF hooks in on-prem harnesses.
- Metrics and assertions: tokens/sec counters, per-request latency histograms, p95/p99 windows, KV cache hit/miss rates, GPU utilization and kernel switch counts; export to Prometheus and a dedicated dashboard.
- Regression detection: baseline snapshotting, rolling-window anomaly detection (z-score + thresholds), and automated regression PR creation with attached artifacts (diffed metrics, flamegraphs, top slow traces).
- Repro artifacts: deterministic trace package (seed, timing, topology), pointer to build SHA, model variant, quantization profile, and a short reproducibility recipe for on-call/CS.

Scope and constraints:
- Must run inside both Redwood Private CI and customer-like VPC testbeds; keep dependencies minimal for on-prem packaging.
- Determinism prioritized for control-plane and request ordering; absolute token timings may be subject to host scheduling — document expected nondeterminism bounds.
- Leverage existing telemetry collectors and the runtime’s trace hooks to avoid invasive instrumentation.

Deliverables:
1) scenario-runner binary with CLI (compile, run, pack)
2) network profile library (prebuilt profiles + composer)
3) Prometheus scrape configs + Grafana dashboard + regression rule templates
4) CI integration job and a cookbook Confluence page for SRE/SE runs

Success criteria:
- Reproduce 90% of customer-reported regressions in VPC testbeds within 3 attempts
- Generate reproducibility package < 200MB for common 1M-token traces
- Alerting for p95 regressions within 10 minutes of run completion

Risks & trade-offs:
- High fidelity network emulation may require kernel modules (eBPF) on some on-prem images — fallback to tc/NetEm supported but less precise.
- Deterministic replay may mask concurrency-induced flakiness; we will provide a non-deterministic mode that preserves original inter-arrival microtiming for debugging.

Successors / follow-ups:
- Integrate with Optimize to recommend batching/quantization changes when regressions persist
- Template-based customer repro snapshots for SE export
comments: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on seeded RNG approach and packaging as single static binary. Action: Marcus to prototype seed injection into runner (ENG-85921-A).

2026-02-18: Prototype: initial CLI that compiles a trace into an execution bundle (seed + request list). Achieved deterministic ordering locally. Observed ~8% variance in p95 between runs due to host CPU throttling. Logged: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-85921+prototype

2026-02-25: Design review with infra and security. Decided to implement network emulation via eBPF on internal images and fall back to tc/NetEm for customer on-prem distributions. Security requested Kconfig opt-in — added to scope.
2026-03-01: Integration: hooked metrics to Prometheus. Initial dashboard: tokens/sec over time, p95 per-window, KV cache hit ratio. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/eng-85921

2026-03-04: Regression detection rules drafted. Rule example: p95 >= baseline * 1.25 && z_score >= 2.5 for 3 consecutive windows => create regression artifact PR. Implemented automated PR creation in CI (see github PR below).

2026-03-07: Dogfood run in private CI against model-2026-02-14-qa: 1M tokens scenario. Results: baseline tokens/sec 18.2k, current run 16.8k (-7.7%). p95 increased from 120ms to 185ms. Regression rule triggered and PR auto-created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2643
2026-03-09: Feedback from SE: reproducibility package too large for multi-day traces. Action: add compression for repeat patterns and option to trim low-signal segments. Tracking subtask ENG-85921-1.
2026-03-10: Security signoff pending for eBPF usage on customer images; SSO & KMS considerations added to runbook. Next: finalize packaging and runbook for partner SEs.
